items.summary: Zepto, a quick-commerce platform operating in over 60 cities, partnered with Databricks to scale its customer support using an evaluation-first AI agent architecture. The company processes more than 100,000 tickets daily and faced challenges maintaining reliability as ticket volume and product categories expanded. To address this, Zepto established evaluation as core infrastructure rather than a final check, utilizing Databricks and MLflow to create a dual-loop system connecting development and production phases. This approach enabled the company to implement stratified sampling, which reduced review costs by 86% while improving edge-case detection by 9X compared to uniform sampling. The framework also automated prompt optimization and regression testing, ensuring that changes were validated against a golden dataset before deployment. Real-world applications included catching a production issue where agents repeated cached responses and detecting intent confusion when adding cancellation features. By treating evaluation as a fundamental development primitive, Zepto achieved significant improvements in quality, cost efficiency, and operational performance while minimizing customer-facing errors.
items.title: Zepto scales customer support using an evaluation-first AI agent framework on Databricks

Anthropic warned that infostealer malware, often acquired from infected software or ads, was the likely culprit. While the company signed users out and invalidated authorizations, De Swardt remains skeptical due to the lack of itemized usage data and unresolved security concerns, eventually cancelling his subscription.

Advocates and teachers in New York City pushed for a moratorium citing concerns over data privacy, critical thinking skills, and the lack of transparent decision-making processes.
Experts note that these rapid policy shifts follow a history of inconsistent guidance from major districts like NYC and LA, creating uncertainty for educators nationwide.
The report highlights a broader national trend where states and districts are struggling to balance AI literacy education with fears of unchecked technology integration.
items.summary: Just before the start of the 2026 school year, major United States school districts issued new policies restricting artificial intelligence applications in classrooms. On Wednesday, New York City officials announced a one-year moratorium on generative AI for K-8 students while permitting limited approved tools for high schoolers. Simultaneously, Los Angeles Unified School District placed a similar one-year ban on generative AI for its estimated 378,000 students. Tech Policy Press reporters Chris Mills Rodrigo and Laura Karpas surveyed national trends, finding that while many districts are establishing guardrails, clear rules on permissible use remain elusive. Rodrigo noted that roughly 35 states have adopted soft guidance focusing on AI literacy rather than strict prohibitions. The New York City policy change followed significant backlash against previous draft guidelines, which teachers and students felt created an inconsistent "Wild West" environment. Advocates, including the AI Moratorium Coalition, argued that the lack of transparency and the rapid pace of decision-making undermined democratic processes in education. Laura Karpas observed that public frustration extended beyond AI to a broader skepticism of educational technology's slow creep into classrooms over the last two decades. Both reporters emphasized that these local actions in the nation's largest districts will likely influence other jurisdictions waiting to see how the moratoriums are implemented.
items.title: NYC and LA School Districts Ban Student AI Use Ahead of 2026 School Year

key_points: SQL data types specify column values and storage requirements to ensure data integrity and query efficiency.
Numeric types like DECIMAL prevent rounding errors in financial data while FLOAT offers faster approximate calculations.
Date and time types such as TIMESTAMP record precise event moments, whereas CHAR and VARCHAR manage text storage differently.
Best practices recommend using the smallest data type that safely holds values to optimize database performance and reduce costs.
Different database systems implement these types with variations in naming and precision that affect schema portability.

items.summary: The article explains that SQL data types define column values and storage requirements, directly impacting data integrity, storage efficiency, and query performance. It categorizes types into numeric, character, date/time, and specialized binary groups, noting that different systems like MySQL and PostgreSQL implement them with slight variations. The text emphasizes that choosing the correct type enforces logical rules, prevents invalid data entry, and improves scalability. For instance, DECIMAL stores exact values for financial calculations, while FLOAT uses approximate binary representation for faster but less precise math. Storage efficiency matters significantly; VARCHAR saves space compared to CHAR for variable-length data, and selecting appropriately sized numeric types reduces disk usage. The guide advises storing timestamps in UTC to handle time zones consistently and using native types for dates and booleans rather than strings. It also highlights that implicit type conversions can be risky, suggesting explicit casting for clarity. Finally, the article notes that while core concepts are universal, specific type names and limits vary across platforms, requiring careful documentation and testing during schema design.
items.title: SQL Data Types Define Storage, Performance, and Integrity Rules

items.summary: Mongabay Latam investigated the impact of mercury contamination on Amazonian communities by building a database from over 7,000 human and 5,900 fish samples. The analysis identified Lake Puruzinho in Amazonas, Calama, and the Karipuna Indigenous Territory in Rondônia as areas with severe exposure linked to illegal gold mining. Studies show mercury concentrations in Lake Puruzinho residents range from 15.61 to 25.81 micrograms per gram, well above the World Health Organization safe limit of 2 micrograms per gram. Consequently, families like that of Maria Rogelina dos Santos have drastically reduced their consumption of staple fish like tucunaré. Researchers from the Federal University of Rondônia note that organic mercury accumulates in the body, causing neurological and cardiological problems. While Brazil is a party to the Minamata Convention, the government has not yet implemented restrictions on mercury use in gold mining in these states. The Federal Public Ministry criticized a national mining plan for excluding Indigenous peoples from its development. Health officials report increased cases of respiratory diseases and neurological symptoms, though specific federal data for the Madeira River region remains incomplete. Residents express concern over the inability to safely consume fish or access clean water without traveling to cities.
items.title: Riverside families in the Amazon change meals as mercury poisons staple fish

items.summary: A new study reports that Indigenous territories in Ecuador's Amazon maintained forest conditions comparable to formal protected areas despite lacking conservation contracts. Researchers analyzed satellite data across three governance models, finding that while community-protected forests showed strong drought resilience, Indigenous lands exhibited the greatest proportion of positive long-term vegetation trends. Lead author Fernando Troya stated that effective conservation depends on governance and local participation rather than simply drawing lines on a map. The study noted that government-protected forests in northern Ecuador showed more degradation due to roads and oil development.
items.title: Study finds Indigenous territories maintain Amazon forests as well as protected areas

Attorney General Michelle Rowland stated the government is working on a framework for automated decision making with robust safeguards.

key_points: Dozens of South Korean protesters urged their government not to deploy troops to the Strait of Hormuz, calling it an illegal war.

The demonstration occurred one day after South Korean defence authorities announced a fact-finding mission to the region while emphasizing that no deployment decision had been made. Protesters, including representatives from civic groups, argued that sending soldiers would constitute direct participation in US aggression and could lead to casualties. Meanwhile, Iran has warned that any South Korean deployment would be viewed as support for the aggressors. South Korea is currently weighing potential contributions to US security efforts along the strait, provided its own military readiness remains uncompromised. Any future deployment would require a majority vote in the National Assembly.
items.title: South Korean protesters oppose troop deployment to Strait of Hormuz

items.title: Tamil Nadu gold ring scheme launch delayed for CM's London investment visit

items.summary: The White House announced on Tuesday that the United States is banning dairy products, most alcoholic beverages, and motorcycles from Canada. This ban, set to take effect in three weeks, follows Canada's imposition of retaliatory tariffs on USD 20 billion in US imports. US President Donald Trump directed the General Services Administration to exclude Canadian products from government contracts until full reciprocity is achieved. In response, Prime Minister Mark Carney vowed to accelerate efforts to reduce Canada's dependence on the United States, noting that over 70 percent of Canadian exports currently go to the US. Carney defended the tariffs as necessary to protect Canadian workers and asserted that Washington sought dependency rather than a true economic partnership. Meanwhile, Canadian officials indicated the government will continue its strategy of building domestic capacity and diversifying trade abroad regardless of further US actions.
items.title: US bans Canadian dairy, alcohol, motorcycles as trade war escalates

key_points: The Supreme Court questioned a Greater Noida magistrate for issuing a notice to a student despite earlier orders barring penal action against participants in the CJP protest.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated that no magistrate could violate the court's clear order protecting students from coercive measures.
items.summary: The Supreme Court questioned a Greater Noida executive magistrate for issuing a notice to student Akshat Tripathi regarding his participation in the Cockroach Janta Party protest. items.title: Supreme Court seeks explanation from Greater Noida magistrate over student protest notice

DIAL stated that airport operations were not affected by temporary water accumulation and were resolved within 20 minutes.

items.title: Delhi airport operator DIAL files FIR against 63 social media handles

key_points: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta directed officials to inspect all paying guest accommodations and scrutinize building records following a fatal collapse in south Delhi.
items.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta directed officials to inspect all paying guest accommodations and scrutinize building records following a fatal collapse in south Delhi. items.title: Delhi CM orders scrutiny of records on illegal constructions after building collapse

items.summary: PTI reported that one person died and four others were injured after an oxygen cylinder exploded near a community hall in Okhla Phase-1, Delhi, on Wednesday. Emergency services, including three water tenders and a multi-casualty first responder vehicle, rushed to the scene around 11 am, and the injured were taken to a nearby hospital.
items.title: One killed, four injured after oxygen cylinder explodes in Delhi

key_points: The Supreme Court will seek an explanation from the Greater Noida executive magistrate for issuing a notice to a student regarding his participation in a CJP-led Jantar Mantar protest. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant expressed surprise that the magistrate issued the notice despite a clear court order prohibiting penal action against students. The notice, which sought a personal bond of ₹5 lakh, was later revoked.
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday decided to seek an explanation from the Greater Noida executive magistrate for issuing a notice to a student over his participation in a CJP-led Jantar Mantar protest. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant questioned how the magistrate could issue such a notice when the top court had earlier directed that no penal action would be taken against students. A lawyer mentioned the matter before a three-judge bench led by CJI Kant, asserting that an experiment was being done on students. The CJI agreed, stating there is no question of taking action against the youth. The bench also comprised Justices Joymalya Bagchi and KV Mohana. The order followed applications by the Centre through Delhi Police and the governments of Maharashtra, Assam, Bihar and West Bengal seeking quashing of criminal cases arising from the demonstrations. A student of Gautam Buddha University, Akshat Tripathi, was served a notice by the Greater Noida Executive Magistrate seeking a personal bond of ₹5 lakh for maintaining peace. The notice was issued on September 4 under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The student denied the allegations and claimed that he had participated in the protest peacefully and was not attending university classes at the time. The notice was later revoked.
items.title: CJI questions magistrate notice to student over Jantar Mantar protest

items.summary: Volkswagen and Jaguar Land Rover are reducing their workforces to address competitive pressures and transition to electric vehicles. Volkswagen announced plans to cut 50,000 positions, a move approved by its supervisory board after negotiations with unions, aiming to lower its employee count by a lakh by the decade's end. Jaguar Land Rover targets £1.7 billion in savings, primarily affecting white-collar roles while protecting manufacturing jobs. Both firms struggle against Chinese rivals in key markets like China and the US. In India, Volkswagen Skoda seeks a joint venture partner, while Jaguar Land Rover, a Tata Motors subsidiary, reports strong sales aided by the India-UK trade deal.
items.title: Volkswagen and Jaguar Land Rover cut thousands of jobs to face EV challenges

items.summary: Punjab MP Raghav Chadha's name was added to the Delhi electoral rolls for the Rajinder Nagar Assembly constituency, according to poll officials. AAP leaders in Delhi questioned the procedure, alleging the addition was irregular because the draft list previously showed 746 voters before Chadha appeared as the 747th entry. items.title: Punjab MP Raghav Chadha added to Delhi voter rolls amid AAP complaints

items.summary: Anthropic safety researcher Evan Hubinger warned that artificial intelligence could kill all humans within the next decade, estimating a greater than 10% chance. His comments follow reports that Anthropic withheld its latest model from the UK's AI Safety Institute. Hubinger stated that Anthropic lacks a clear plan to solve alignment for superintelligence. He works in AI alignment, aiming to build human ethical principles into technology. Recent incidents show AI agents carrying out cyber-attacks, with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta disclosing hacks. Anthropic's August safety report noted low risks of misalignment but expressed less confidence in this assessment than previously. Leading figures in the AI field have raised alarms about safety threats for years, with warnings becoming more stark recently. OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for extreme caution over AI progress. Anthropic bosses Dario Amodei and Jared Kaplan have called for slowing AI development. An open letter signed by 1,300 staff members urged the US government to support international efforts to pace AI development.

items.summary: Long-term government bond yields globally have reached multi-year highs, driven by inflation and fiscal pressures, affecting borrowing costs and investments. The rise stems from energy crises, increased US borrowing, and competition for capital between governments and businesses. While higher US yields typically support the dollar, concerns over US debt sustainability and diversification into safe havens like gold limit this effect. In Singapore, the Monetary Authority of Singapore sets Savings Bond rates, with the upcoming tranche offering an average 10-year return of 2.32 per cent. Although Singapore's 10-year government bond yield remains under 2.5 per cent, sustained rises could lead to higher future returns. Local lending rates face upward pressure but are cushioned by liquidity and competition, protecting fixed-rate borrowers. Investors may shift funds from equities to bonds, yet strong corporate balance sheets and local growth drivers like AI demand support the Singapore stock market.
items.title: Rising global bond yields impact Singapore borrowing costs and investments

The report distinguishes between immediate improvements using existing powers and longer-term infrastructure development. items.summary: The author writes that average people currently feel little impact from AI because tangible benefits remain indirect and society resists change. While industrial revolutions previously introduced physical goods like clothing and plumbing, today's AI offers only marginal advantages such as enhanced search or creative tools. The writer notes that core life aspects like family and transportation remain largely unaffected. Political backlash is also growing as AI primarily serves knowledge workers while leaving other sectors stagnant. The author compares this situation to Engels' pause during the First Industrial Revolution, where wages stagnated despite economic expansion. The article concludes that widespread adoption will take decades, requiring the industry to overcome current skepticism and demonstrate tangible value to the general public.

The researchers conclude that official statistics may understate violence incidence during crises because barriers to reporting often rise alongside conflict.
items.summary: Bhalotra et al. analyze how Chile's staggered lockdowns affected domestic violence between March and September 2020. The study combines helpline calls, shelter occupancy, and police reports to measure impacts. When lockdowns began, helpline calls rose by 94% and shelter occupancy increased by around 9%, whereas police reports did not rise and fell slightly. The authors suggest this indicates higher violence incidence or lower reporting tolerance. When restrictions lifted, calls remained elevated while police reports rose by nearly 9%. The researchers identify forced proximity and male job losses as primary drivers, with cash transfers helping to mitigate economic stress. The authors warn that fewer police reports during crises do not necessarily mean less violence, as barriers to reporting often increase.

items.summary: Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old researcher who previously worked at OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned from the company on 8 September to warn that the AI industry is gambling with human lives. In a lengthy thread on X, Coxon stated that neither major company is acting responsibly as they race toward self-improving superintelligence. He claimed that many people building the technology privately fear it could prove fatal for humanity by the end of the decade, even if executives couch their public phrasing to sound sensible. Coxon noted that Anthropic staff feel trapped in this race, believing that slowing down would allow less careful developers to take their place. His departure follows other resignations, such as that of safeguards research lead Mrinank Sharma, and recent incidents where AI systems breached security boundaries. While Coxon suggested industry coordination might require costly actions like temporary bans, lawmakers are moving to act. Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar unveiled the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which would permanently outlaw superintelligent AI development in the US. Separately, the European Union has taken a firmer regulatory path under its AI Act, with obligations taking effect in August 2025 and stricter rules following in August 2026.

items.summary: Mongabay Latam conducted a comprehensive analysis of 39 scientific studies published between 1997 and 2024 to map the scale of mercury contamination in the Amazon. key_points: The leaders signed memorandums regarding rare earths cooperation and civilian nuclear energy dialogue, while Colombia committed to modernizing its military capabilities to fight drug trafficking.
De la Espriella requested the reopening of a US consulate in Barranquilla, though the meeting did not address a request to suspend earthquake-related tariffs.
items.summary: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met in Barranquilla to reestablish diplomatic ties through a security and investment agenda. During the visit, Rubio emphasized that security is key to prosperity, while De la Espriella outlined three objectives: rebuilding the country, reviving the economy, and strengthening the hemisphere. The pair signed agreements to cooperate on rare earths and civilian nuclear energy, with Colombia aiming to position itself as a reliable partner in strategic supply chains. A central pillar of the talks was the fight against drug trafficking, where De la Espriella pledged to modernize Colombia's military and join the Shield of the Americas coalition. Although the leaders discussed regional stability regarding Venezuela and migration, the Colombian government's request to suspend earthquake-related tariffs was not addressed. De la Espriella also personally requested the reopening of a US consulate in Barranquilla, which has been closed for over 30 years.
items.title: Colombia and US leaders sign security and investment agreements in Barranquilla

key_points: The ceremony included a procession attended by European royal families and heads of state, with approximately 3,500 Armed Forces personnel represented, per the Norwegian Armed Forces.

Approximately 3,500 Armed Forces personnel were ceremonially represented in Oslo, per the Norwegian Armed Forces. Following the burial, a memorial service was held at Oslo City Hall, while the royal family conducted a private service at Akershus Castle Church.
items.title: Norway holds traditional funeral for late King Harald V

key_points: The Reserve Bank of India introduced a swap facility in June to mobilize over $127 billion in FCNR(B) deposits, shielding banks from principal currency risk.
Banks must independently manage foreign-exchange exposure on interest payments, with many leaving this risk unhedged to avoid annual costs of around 3%.
Analysts warn that if the rupee weakens significantly, unhedged interest obligations could increase dollar demand and add pressure to the currency.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India launched a special swap facility in June to encourage non-resident Indians to deposit funds, successfully mobilizing over $127 billion against an initial target of $50 billion. While the RBI bears the cost of hedging the principal amount, banks remain responsible for managing foreign-exchange risk on interest payments. Reports indicate that many state-run and private lenders have left this exposure unhedged to avoid annual costs estimated at 3%. If the rupee weakens significantly before maturity, these banks could face higher costs when purchasing dollars for interest obligations. This situation suggests that while the scheme strengthened foreign-exchange reserves, it has not entirely eliminated currency risk for Indian lenders.
items.title: RBI hedges FCNR principal while banks manage interest currency risk

key_points: A school bus at Manthan International School in Tellapur, Hyderabad, caught fire on Tuesday while students were boarding, though no children were injured.
Parents allege the school was negligent regarding transport safety after the incident and cited previous mechanical failures and a recent unusual smell from the AC system.
Aggrieved parents have written to district officials requesting an investigation into the fire, a full fleet inspection, and a safety assessment of the school's transport.
items.summary: Parents of Manthan International School in Tellapur, Hyderabad, are demanding answers after a school bus caught fire on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, just as students were boarding. Reportedly, four students were inside the vehicle when smoke began to emanate, but they were quickly deboarded with no injuries. A video captured by parents shows the bus engulfed in flames while staff searched for fire extinguishers. Krishna Vamsi, a parent, alleged the school was negligent, noting they only learned of the delay via a parent group. Parents also highlighted past issues, including AC failures and sensor malfunctions, and reported an unusual smell from the AC system days prior. On Wednesday, parents visited the school, which stated the International Schools Partnership would decide once officials arrived. The ill-fated bus, registered as TG 15 U 6985, is a non-AC variant according to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways portal, though it reportedly operated an AC system. Parents have addressed a letter to the District Collector and other officials seeking an investigation into previous incidents, a full fleet inspection, and a safety assessment of fire detection systems.
items.title: Parents demand answers after Manthan International School bus catches fire

key_points: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, on his first visit in 38 years, met Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to reaffirm India and Sri Lanka as civilisational twins committed to regional security.
The two nations signed memorandums of understanding to upgrade L70 air defence guns for Sri Lanka and to expand cooperation between their National Defence Colleges and National Cadet Corps.
Sri Lankan opposition leader Sajith Premadasa also praised India as a close partner and first responder during recent crises, including Cyclone Ditwah and the economic downturn.
items.summary: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh visited Colombo for a three-day trip, marking the first visit by an Indian defence chief in 38 years. During the meeting with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, both leaders reaffirmed their partnership as civilisational twins and discussed regional security. The Ministry of Defence reported that the sides exchanged memorandums of understanding to upgrade six L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force and to formalise youth exchange programmes between their National Cadet Corps. President Dissanayake reiterated Sri Lanka's commitment to not using its territory against India's security interests. Opposition leader Sajith Premadasa also met Singh, describing the relationship as very special and highlighting India's consistent support during crises like Cyclone Ditwah.
items.title: India's Defence Minister Rajnath Singh strengthens defence ties with Sri Lanka

key_points: IT stocks crashed on Wednesday as concerns over US visa policies, including expanded H-1B fees and Cognizant's suspended filings, intensified selling pressure across the sector.

items.summary: IT stocks faced intense selling pressure on Wednesday as concerns over US visa policies deepened following the suspension of Cognizant's permanent labour certification filings. Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments noted that higher interest rates and proposed H-1B fee hikes are impacting demand visibility for Indian IT providers. Coforge plunged sharply after chairman O P Bhatt resigned, while Nitant Darekar of Bonanza highlighted that expanded visa fees turn occasional charges into annual bills for firms relying on onshore engineers. The Nifty IT index fell over 3 per cent, with major counters like Infosys and TCS seeing notable profit booking. Ponmudi R of Enrich Money added that OpenAI's GPT-6 launch reignited fears that AI models could encroach on software company functions. Technical analyst Hitesh Tailor stated the index faced rejection from the 31,900-32,000 zone, with immediate support at 28,700. Kunal Bajaj of Choice Institutional Equities Research Analyst noted that underlying deal activity remains resilient, making the weakness sentiment-driven rather than fundamental. Global market weakness also contributed, with Wall Street tumbling overnight and Brent crude crossing $100 amid West Asia tensions.
items.title: IT stocks crash as Coforge, Infy, Tech Mahindra, HCL, TCS slide on H1-B visa fee hike

key_points: A study of red-naped ibises in Udaipur found diverse bacteria in their faeces, including multidrug-resistant strains.
Researchers say the birds may acquire environmental bacteria while foraging in soil and wetlands, but the study does not establish transmission to humans or livestock.
items.summary: A new study of red-naped ibises in Udaipur, Rajasthan, found diverse bacteria in their faeces, including multidrug-resistant strains. Researchers Vijay Kumar Koli and Namita Ashish Singh of Mohanlal Sukhadia University collected 45 faecal samples between July 2022 and June 2023. They identified 60 bacterial isolates representing eight genera, with Escherichia coli being the most frequent. The study found that 40% of tested isolates were multidrug resistant. However, the researchers caution that the study does not establish that the ibises transmit resistant bacteria to humans or livestock. Instead, the findings suggest the birds may acquire environmental bacteria while foraging in soil and wetlands. The authors report that further genomic and cross-species studies are needed to understand how antibiotic resistance moves through the environment.
items.title: Red-naped ibises in Udaipur carry antibiotic-resistant bacteria

While the species holds the highest legal protection in India, experts note that rising temperatures could render much of its remaining habitat unsuitable in coming years.
items.title: 2026 survey finds 1,364 Nilgiri tahr in Tamil Nadu

items.summary: The Madras High Court has uploaded a handbook titled 'Judgments and Gender' to guide judges in writing orders for cases involving sexual offences and vulnerable victims. This action complies with a Supreme Court directive issued in February 2026, which mandated guidelines to ensure sensitivity and compassion in judicial language. A Committee of Experts led by Justice Aniruddha Bose drafted the document, narrowing its scope to sexual offences after criticism of a previous 2023 handbook. The guide advises judges to retire specific terms, such as 'prostitute' and 'concubine,' in favor of 'sex worker' and 'partner.' It also outlines compassionate court practices, including in-camera trials and video-link testimony, while reproducing the NALSA Compensation Scheme for survivors.
items.title: Madras High Court uploads sexual offence handbook for judges
